title: Q4 prefill QuantizedMatmul on the Honeykrisp 8x8x8 fp32 cooperative matrix, gated by capability

change.scope: QuantizedMatmul, matrix_m > 1, transposed affine 4-bit / group-64, f16 x and output (the Qwen2.5-0.5B-4bit layout); decode (matrix_m == 1), other bit widths, group sizes, dtypes, and the non-transposed layout are untouched
change.design: one 32-lane subgroup per workgroup owns a 32x32 output tile as 4x4 fp32 8x8 accumulators; per 8-wide k step the lanes stage the x rows as f32 (unpackHalf2x16 from a 32-bit word view) and the weight block dequantized once (the REGISTER_BLOCK qmm_tile.comp packed-word unpack, one scale/bias load per 64-wide group) into 2 KiB of shared memory; coopMatLoad reads both from shared, 16 coopMatMulAdd per step; the finished tile drains through shared one 8-row block at a time, rounds to f16 once, and masks the m and n tails
change.numerics: dequantized weights stay f32 inside the dot (the qmm_tile.comp contract); the matrix unit sums the 8-wide products in its own order, so there is no bitwise pin against the tile - the host-reference bound is the contract
change.gate: existing register-block gate (MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_TILE and _RB not '0', float16 output, transpose_, bits 4, group 64) && cooperative_matrix_f32_8 && subgroup_size == 32 && 2 KiB <= max_compute_shared_memory_size && lhs_offset % 2 == 0 && output_offset % 2 == 0 && !MLX_OMARCHY_NO_COOPMAT; every other case dispatches QmmTileRbF16 exactly as before. No new env switch.
files: overlay/tests/omarchy/test_matmul_family.cpp (new case; register-block bitwise pin skipped on a coopmat device)

occupancy_finding.first_cut: staged a whole 64-wide k chunk per subgroup: x_s 32x64 + w_s 64x32 + o_s 32x32 floats = 20 KiB shared. Correct (same host-reference errors) but 0.55x the register-blocked tile in bench_decode prefill (short 97.3 -> 78.7, long 254.4 -> 158.1, ctx1024 272.6 -> 169.4 tok/s, five pairs each) and 126-154 GFLOP/s in the microbenchmark against the tile's 211-279. Threadgroup memory bounds occupancy on AGX (32 KiB per core), so 20 KiB per 32-lane workgroup left one subgroup per core.
occupancy_finding.kept: 2 KiB shared (one 32x8 x step + one 8x32 weight step, output drained through x_s): 764-832 GFLOP/s at m=1053 in the same microbenchmark. Do not re-try the big-shared design; the win is occupancy, not the MMA.

test.case: qmm coopmat prefill matches host reference at Qwen shapes
test.bound: the qmm tile anchor bound: (3k + 1) * 2 * max_abs * 2^-23 + 2 * max_abs * 2^-11 (same derivation and tolerance as 'qmm tile matches host reference and qmm.comp across prefill shapes'; not loosened)
test.tile_vs_host_same_case: identical to three digits on every shape (llvmpipe and M1 stock legs); the difference is in the f16 output rounding of the same sums
test.register_block_case_on_coopmat_device: candidate_vs_baseline_max 0 at k in {64, 128, 192} (bitwise equal after f16 rounding); the CHECK_EQ pin is only asserted off a coopmat device

benchmark.method: scripts/bench_decode.py through a throwaway driver (/tmp/qmmcm_bench.py on the M1, not committed): mlx-community/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-4bit revision a5339a4131f135d0fdc6a5c8b5bbed2753bbe0f3, the three README prefill workloads from scripts/bench_matrix.json (short 'Hi' 30 prompt tokens / 32 generated, long 262 / 128, ctx1024 1053 / 32), MLX_DISABLE_COMPILE=1, greedy, seed 0, 4 warm-up tokens, --wheel provenance gate. Five alternating process pairs per workload on the coopmat ICD: gate off (MLX_OMARCHY_NO_COOPMAT=1) then gate on, plus one stock Mesa 26.1.7 process per workload. Each pair waited for the 1-minute load average below 1.5 (observed 0.00-0.43 before every pair, 0.07-0.43 after) with no model or test process running; AC power on. Medians of five; paired gain is the median of the five on/off ratios.
benchmark.wheel: dist/mlx_omarchy-0.32.2.dev202609081308+5935a01-cp314-cp314-linux_aarch64.whl (scripts/build-wheel.sh with DEV_RELEASE=1 MLX_OMARCHY_SOURCE_COMMIT=5935a01; provenance line 'mlx-omarchy 0.32.2.dev202609081308+5935a01 ... verified=match libmlx.so=sha256:f97519fcfe96223b' on every run; both sides of every pair are the same wheel with the env toggle, which is the intended A/B here)

limitations: Only the transposed affine 4-bit/group-64 f16 prefill path; other quantization modes, bf16/f32 activations, the non-transposed layout, and decode keep their current kernels.
Stock Mesa 26.1.7 users get the register-blocked tile until the honeykrisp-coopmat branch merges upstream; the capability is false there and on llvmpipe.
The 30-token prefill gains only 1.17x: with one 32-row tile the 896-wide projections dispatch 28 subgroups, too few to fill the GPU; a k-split or a narrower tile at small m is the next lever.
An f16-A/B variant on the 16x16x16 shape (hk/coopmat-shapes) was considered and rejected with Main: it would round scale*q+bias to f16 before the product, which the qmm kernels explicitly refuse.
The bench driver and microbenchmark binaries were built outside CMake from the same tree; they are not committed.
